title: Pullback image of products by recursive ideal powers
statement: Let $f:X\to Y$ be a morphism of schemes, $J$ a quasi-coherent ideal sheaf on $Y$, $G$ a quasi-coherent $\mathcal O_Y$-module, and $n\ge 0$. Let $T=f^*$ [def-pc-module-pullback], $I=J\mathcal O_X$ [def-nagata-extended-ideal], and use the recursive module-subobject powers and ideal-module products of [def-weil-pbc-coherent-formal-module]. Then the image subobject of $T(J^nG\hookrightarrow G)$ equals the image subobject of $I^n T(G)\hookrightarrow T(G)$ inside $T(G)$. At $n=0$ the power is the full structure sheaf.

source.place: Tag 0887, displayed quotient computation in the proof; checked against https://stacks.math.columbia.edu/tag/0887

proof.text: On affine V in Y and affine U contained in its inverse image, write A = O_Y(V), B = O_X(U), a = J(V), M = G(V). The recursive module ideal power has sections a^n and the indicated inclusion: n=0 is the structure-sheaf identity; n=1 is the ideal inclusion; at n+1 the ideal-product formula and its multiplication inclusion give a times a^n = a^(n+1). Identify this quasi-coherent power subobject with the sheaf for the ideal-data power J^n by equality of the inclusions on the affine basis. Applying the ideal-product formula to J^n and G now identifies J^n G with a^n M, compatibly with its inclusion in M.

The affine tensor-pullback comparison and its naturality identify the pulled-back product inclusion with B tensor_A a^n M -> B tensor_A M. Its image is generated by tensors b tensor c m with c in a^n. The extended ideal has affine sections a B, and extension commutes with powers. Thus this image equals (a B)^n times B tensor_A M: generators give one inclusion, and expanding products of generators of a B gives the reverse inclusion. For n=0 both submodules are the whole tensor product.

The affine power and product formula on X identifies this same submodule with the image of the recursive-power product inclusion into f*G. Powers, products, their pullbacks, and the images of morphisms between quasi-coherent modules are quasi-coherent; consequently the sheaf images have precisely these sectionwise images on affine opens. These pairs U,V form a basis, by choosing an affine neighborhood of f(x) and then an affine neighborhood of x inside its preimage. Equal submodules on this basis give equal subobjects of f*G: membership is local, so each subobject inclusion factors through the other and the factorizations agree on overlaps by monicity. Gluing produces both inclusions and hence equality. The formulas remain valid for empty opens, the zero module and the zero and unit ideals.
